oracles.claim: A signature produced by ML-DSA Sign with a valid key and context shall verify under the matching public key.
limitations: Verification success is a functional relation, not a EUF-CMA security result

controls.positive_control: the signature is produced from a freshly generated key pair
controls.negative_control: a one-byte signature mutation is rejected by the negative oracle

oracles.claim: Two conforming ML-DSA implementations exchanging public keys and signatures shall cross-verify for the same profile and context.
limitations: Cross-verification must use an identical pure/prehash and context profile
A self-reference pair does not establish independent correctness

controls.negative_control: a signature from a different key does not verify

oracles.claim: A mutated ML-DSA signature component shall not verify under the signing public key.
limitations: Exact-length, hint canonicality, and norm boundaries require their dedicated oracles
This oracle does not prove sUF-CMA

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the signature bytes changed

oracles.claim: A signature shall not verify for a message that differs from the signed message.
limitations: Message equality in the verifier domain is not tested across all message encodings

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the message bytes changed

oracles.claim: A signature shall not verify when the verification context differs from the signing context.
limitations: Adapters without context support return API_UNSUPPORTED and are not failures
Context boundary lengths 0/1/254/255/256 are not covered by this oracle

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the context bytes changed

oracles.claim: HashML-DSA verification shall reject a prehash object whose OID differs from the signing OID.
limitations: Disabled until a HashML-DSA prehash interface is available
OID substitution must not be simulated by appending bytes to the context

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the OID bytes changed

oracles.claim: Hedged ML-DSA signing shall consume the supplied randomness so that distinct randomness streams produce distinct signatures.
limitations: Deterministic profiles legitimately ignore ambient randomness
Reported RNG failure handling is a separate oracle

controls.positive_control: distinct deterministic tapes are observed to be consumed

oracles.claim: ML-DSA verification shall return false for every signature length that differs from the profile signature length, including empty, L-1, L+1 with 0x00, L+1 with 0xA5, and oversized signatures.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Sections 3.6.2 and 5.3; DeepSeek design doc Section 29.3
limitations: Public-key exact length is enforced by the wrapper when the raw API has no pk length parameter
Truncations at every component boundary are sampled, not exhaustive

controls.negative_control: each boundary mutation record shows a changed signature length

oracles.claim: ML-DSA context lengths 0, 1, 254, and 255 shall sign and verify, context length 256 shall be rejected at the signing boundary, and a different verification context shall not verify.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 5.2 (context string) and DeepSeek design doc Section 29.8
limitations: Adapters without an extended-context boundary record NOT_APPLICABLE
Applications that never expose context are out of scope for the boundary subtest

controls.negative_control: a mismatched context does not verify

oracles.claim: ML-DSA verification shall reject non-canonical hint encodings: cumulative counts that decrease or exceed omega, non-increasing positions within a polynomial, and non-zero unused position bytes.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 7.2 Algorithm 21 HintBitUnpack; DeepSeek design doc Section 29.4
limitations: Each mutation class is applied once to a valid signature; a survivor is a test-gap signal, not a forgery
All three parameter sets share the same mutation classes

controls.negative_control: each mutation record shows the hint bytes changed

oracles.claim: ML-DSA verification shall reject signatures whose response coefficients reach or exceed the norm bound gamma1 - beta, including the negative boundary.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 5.3 (norm check) and DeepSeek design doc Section 29.6
limitations: The valid-boundary mutation (gamma1 - beta - 1) breaks the challenge relation, so a rejection there is expected for an unrelated reason; that subtest is a structural observation
Only the first packed response coefficient is rewritten

controls.negative_control: each mutation record shows the packed coefficient changed

oracles.claim: Hedged ML-DSA signing shall reproduce byte-identical signatures under a fixed zero randomness tape, and distinct randomness tapes shall produce distinct signatures that every verify.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 3.4 (hedged and deterministic signing) and DeepSeek design doc Section 29.7
limitations: The fixed zero tape is an external approximation of the internal fixed-rnd validation interface
Deterministic profiles legitimately skip the fresh-randomness subtest

controls.negative_control: distinct tapes are observed to be consumed

oracles.claim: A pure ML-DSA signature and a prehash ML-DSA signature for the same message shall not verify in each other's domain.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 5.4 and DeepSeek design doc Section 29.8
limitations: No prehash interface is exposed by the selected adapters; recorded NOT_APPLICABLE rather than simulated

controls.positive_control: a pure signature verifies in the pure domain
controls.negative_control: the record is not persisted as a finding

oracles.claim: Prehash verification shall reject a digest whose OID differs from the signing OID.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Section 5.4 and DeepSeek design doc Section 29.8
limitations: No prehash/OID interface is exposed; recorded NOT_APPLICABLE

controls.positive_control: a matching prehash OID verifies when a prehash API exists
controls.negative_control: the record is not persisted as a finding

oracles.claim: A reported RNG failure during ML-DSA key generation or signing should produce a failure indication and no signature output rather than proceeding with zeroed randomness.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 204 Sections 3.4 and 3.6 and DeepSeek design doc Sections 22 and 28.9
limitations: Void RNG APIs cannot report failure; continuing is a hardening gap

controls.positive_control: the same call succeeds without the injected failure
controls.negative_control: the failure tape is observed to be consumed
